frequency_question: How often does a nation successfully stand up a domestic production line for complex guided munitions within 24 months during wartime?
membership_rule: Includes sovereign states attempting to localize production of foreign-designed guided missiles, rockets, or precision weapons during active high-intensity conflict.

cases.name: UK wartime dispersal of aircraft and guided weapon component manufacturing (1940-1943)
Soviet relocation of defense manufacturing to the Urals (1941-1942)
Taiwan Hsiung Feng missile domestic production scaling under PRC threat (1970s-1980s)
Iran domestic anti-ship missile production under Iraq war sanctions/attacks (1984-1988)

provenance_note: 5 cases named, 7 claimed via skeleton x multiplier (1.4x)
coverage_note: 5 named; believed roughly 7 in total for high-intensity state-backed missile localization attempts.
known_gaps: Classified or obscure domestic missile programs in smaller conflicts (e.g., specific non-state or proxy localizations) are omitted due to lack of verifiable public records.
skeleton: Total wartime localized complex weapons manufacturing initiatives identified in major conflicts since WWII.
multiplier: 5 hits out of 7 major historical instances of attempted wartime tech transfer and domestic missile/precision-guided munitions line setup.
validity_reason: Industrial base resilience patterns and modern additive manufacturing/CNC transfer speeds remain structurally stable over multi-decade horizons.
